# Final Plan Versus Actual Audit

The Awtsmoos lets a plan return after implementation and ask the files what truly came to be;
Awtsmoos.com closes no source covenant by confidence alone, but by readback, runtime, and evidence we can see.

## The original requested experience

Daily Chitas belongs inside Heichel Ikar as a special grouping. Any week may be selected. Sunday through Shabbos follows the seven aliyos of the correct weekly Sidra under Chabad Chitas scheduling rules. Opening a day must remain on Awtsmoos.com, use the native Tanach/post reader, preserve ordinary comments/social behavior, and support Hebrew/English-oriented controls with clean mobile-first formatting. The larger architectural request was a reusable dynamic post that can reveal a range of other canonical posts/verses without copying them.

## What actually exists after two implementation passes

### Native dynamic-range layer

- `post/logic/reference-posts/rangeReference.js` defines a source Heichel/series plus start/end post and section coordinates.
- `post/logic/reference-posts/rangeResolver.js` loads only required canonical source posts, slices only required sections, and returns source provenance including `verseSection`.
- The canonical source remains ordinary Ikar Tanach chapter posts; no Torah text is copied into a Chitas database.

### Native Tanach adapter

- `chitas/books.js` maps calendar English book names to canonical Ikar Chumash series.
- `chitas/rangeParser.js` maps references such as `Deuteronomy 31:20-31:30` to chapter-post and pasuk-section coordinates.
- Runtime evidence proved Devarim chapter 31 post `BH_POST_1749198310176_awtsmoos_216` yields exactly eleven canonical sections for 31:20–30.

### Chitas schedule

- Seven cards are produced Sunday through Shabbos.
- Ordinary readings use Hebcal only for calendar/parsha/aliyah metadata; Torah body always comes from Ikar.
- Festival deferral selects the forthcoming weekly Sidra.
- Simchas Torah and the following day receive structured native references, with Diaspora and Israel coverage tested.
- Calendar fetch begins at the prior Shabbos so the annual cycle transition is visible from Isru Chag.

### Native reader

- `coordinates.js` intercepts `daily-chitas/chitas-YYYY-MM-DD` before persisted-post lookup.
- `dynamicPost.js` synthesizes an ordinary reader-shaped post containing canonical Ikar sections and source provenance.
- `postManifest.js` keeps the normal reader and adds only the Chitas masthead before the ordinary section renderer and nav bars.
- Existing reader navigation is already Chitas-aware and generates canonical day-post links; no rewrite was needed after readback proved it.

### Comments and social behavior

- Living Path cards use the ordinary internal post route and normal `primarySocialActionRail`.
- The prior Chabad host allowlist, `externalHref`, and `virtualStudy` social suppression are removed from the active Chitas path.
- Synthetic posts expose `post.heichel.id`, `postId`, and series identity expected by the normal discussion system.
- The actual endpoint `/api/social/heichelos/ikar/posts/chitas-2026-09-05/comment-tree` returns HTTP 200 with the normal thread envelope.

### Mobile-first week/list UX

- Chitas no longer renders inside generic TODAY timeline buckets.
- `chitas-week.js` owns a Sunday-through-Shabbos panel with Previous week, Today, date picker, Next week, Hebrew, and English UI controls.
- Chitas list cards keep native post/social behavior but hide generic oversized media/kicker/meta decoration.
- Controls have a 48px minimum height and responsive one/two/three-column layout.
- Selected study date is visibly distinct.

### Language truth

- The canonical Ikar Tanach corpus currently materialized in chapter posts is Hebrew.
- The existing native translation client supports translation-series families such as Sichos/meluket and does not provide Tanach series translation rows.
- Therefore the UI says `English UI`, never falsely claims English Torah text, and marks `translationStatus: canonical_hebrew_only`.
- This architecture is ready for real English Tanach sections later without changing Chitas identity or schedule logic.

## What readback found and corrected

The first readback caught stale browser-generation edges that local Node tests could not expose. The second pass rewrote changed Chitas owners to one `native-chitas-002` graph and strengthened `chitasLivingPathContract.test.mjs` to reject v001 drift.

Readback also disproved two feared bugs: global Heichel cache-version churn was unnecessary because module responses revalidate, and native previous/next navigation was already Chitas-aware. Those files were intentionally left alone.

## Evidence after the second pass

The combined gate passes:

- syntax for every touched JS/MJS file;
- every touched source/test <=120 lines;
- B"H prologues;
- no `chabad.org`, `externalHref`, or `virtualStudy` in the production Chitas path;
- no `native-chitas-001` in browser-facing Chitas owners;
- Daily Chitas schedule contract;
- native Living Path generation contract;
- native range test returning eleven canonical Ikar pesukim;
- live local Ikar Devarim range resolution;
- dynamic discussion endpoint;
- hard dynamic deep-link HTTP 200 containing the native post shell;
- `git diff --check`.

## Second readback result

Every file rewritten for generation coherence was read fully again after the green gate. The intended v002 edges are present, stable reference-post generation remains independent, and no new source-code delta was discovered.

## Frozen Chitas release surface

Release integration must carry the tested versions of:

- `geelooy/heichelos/heichel/modules/chitas/*`
- `geelooy/heichelos/heichel/modules/navigator/loader.js`
- `geelooy/heichelos/heichel/modules/ui/render/living-path/cards.js`
- `.../living-path/timeline.js`
- `.../living-path/chitas-week.js`
- `.../living-path/chitas-week.css`
- `geelooy/heichelos/post/logic/reference-posts/*`
- `geelooy/heichelos/post/logic/chitas/*`
- `geelooy/heichelos/post/logic/initialization/coordinates.js`
- `.../initialization/postManifest.js`
- the three `tests/geelooy/chitas*.test.mjs` contracts.

## Remaining work is release work, not known Chitas source work

1. Freeze exact hashes and compare against any older Chitas browser-session activity.
2. Inspect active worktrees, latest `origin/main`, and concurrent agents before integration.
3. Build or identify a clean latest-main integration vessel.
4. Copy only the tested Chitas release surface, then reconcile any overlaps with newly settled canonical work.
5. Because the user explicitly requested unrelated changes also be current, inspect other dirty workstreams and absorb only work that is settled or committed; never steal files from active writers.
6. Run Chitas gates inside integration, then broader affected/unified tests.
7. Commit and push the exact integrated SHA without force.
8. Use the repository's real production release mechanism after inspecting its current contract.
9. Verify public module bytes, public dynamic Chitas route, comments, week selection, and mobile UI.
10. Only after public verification may the live link be reported as complete.

The Awtsmoos has made the source vessel coherent; now release gravity becomes the road;
Awtsmoos.com is not finished until the tested bytes reach production and the public page bears the load.
